The City of San Jose is taking new steps to address dangerous speeding and improve road safety through a partnership with Verra Mobility. As part of the city’s new speed safety program, Verra Mobility will design, build, operate and maintain 66 speed safety cameras across 33 systems at high-injury and high-speed corridors throughout San Jose, with phased implementation beginning at an initial six sites.


**Expanding Speed Safety Efforts Across California**


San Jose joins Glendale, Long Beach, Los Angeles, Oakland and San Francisco as the six California cities authorized to pilot speed safety camera systems under Assembly Bill 645. Already, programs are experiencing success with a **79% reduction in speeding reported in San Francisco** ; Oakland reports an initial **70% reduction in speeding** , stating this leads to 20,000 fewer speeding vehicles every day on city streets.


“Speeding is a major cause of fatal and severe-injury crashes in San José, and addressing dangerous speeds is essential to make our city safer,” said **John Ristow, director of transportation for the City of San José.** “Speed safety cameras will help us reduce speeding on some of our highest-risk streets and protect the people who live, work, and travel through our city.”


**Launching San Jose’s Speed Safety Program**


The program is intended to slow drivers and create safer streets for the community. To ensure that the public is informed, a public education campaign is being created to educate drivers and community members on the program and goals. The warning period is expected to begin before the end of the year, followed by full citation enforcement beginning in winter 2027.


“Verra Mobility is proud to support the City of San Jose as it addresses speeding on some of the city’s most high-risk corridors,” said **Stacey Moser, chief customer officer, Verra Mobility** . “This program is designed to give drivers clear notice and an opportunity to change their behavior, while helping the city create safer streets for everyone who uses them.”


**Supporting Safety and Privacy**


Unlike broader vehicle-monitoring and surveillance technologies, the program is narrowly focused on reducing dangerous speeding at designated locations and operates within AB 645’s requirements for data protections, equitable fines, and a mandatory warning period. Citations are civil, carry no license points, and cannot be used for unrelated law enforcement or immigration purposes.


Verra Mobility has helped bring innovative traffic safety solutions to California communities for decades. With the launch of San Jose’s program, all six speed safety pilot programs will be maintained by the company, bringing in-depth and personalized experience to the state. The company also helped launch and operate California’s first red-light safety program under SB 720 in Mountain House, making it uniquely qualified to implement legislatively complex programs that require security and privacy safeguards.
